newsitem.title: USA: Power deregulation in Mich. may impact credits.
newsitem.headline: Power deregulation in Mich. may impact credits.

text.p: Recommendations to deregulate investor-owned utilities in Michigan could impact the credit quality of public power utilities in the state, Moody's Investors Service reported Friday in its Credit Perspectives publication.

The rating agency said a recently released report by the Michigan Public Service Commission that recommended deregulation of investor-owned utilities could also effect public utilities -- Michigan South Central Power Agency, Michigan Public Power Agency's Belle River and Campbell projects and some of the larger municipal electric systems.
That is because public utilities may face greater competition and the loss of some autonomy in regards to transmission facilities, the rating agency noted.

Moody's said that in the face of deregulation, the public-power agencies "must reduce their fixed costs and maintain adequate financial flexibility, while the municipal participants must also maintain competitive retail rates."
Moody's said it rates $800 million of public power debt in Michigan.
